subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add a native generic provider key/profile quota-bucket routing contract for Gemini-style project quotas, and should it live in core provider/auth fallback or outside core as a plugin/sidecar seam?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config, auth-profile routing, cooldown scope, provider selection, status/probe behavior, and upgrade semantics, so automation should not invent the product boundary.

options.title: Design native bucket-aware provider pools
options.body: Keep this issue open and define bucket metadata, cooldown scope, doctor/docs behavior, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Provider-Pool Tracker
options.body: Treat this as an acceptance criterion under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41135 while preserving this issue's Gemini project-bucket evidence.

options.title: Keep it external for now
options.body: Document current flat key rotation and let sidecars or plugins manage project buckets until a missing core extension API is identified.

recommendation.title: Design native bucket-aware provider pools
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define bucket metadata, cooldown scope, doctor/docs behavior, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses current-main auth config, provider routing, docs, and compatibility policy, where Peter Steinberger has the strongest history signal among inspected owners.
